title: cleanroom-ci-orbit-consolidate-bootseq-and-dep-prune
author: Evan Turner
description: Motivation: CI feedback latency and flakiness have been steadily impacting developer velocity. This PR consolidates the CI 'boot sequence' steps into a deterministic, idempotent initializer, removes duplicated setup logic across multiple workflows, and introduces a conservative automated dependency pruning pass that removes unused top-level dev deps and surfaces suspects for manual review. Changes are limited to CI orchestration, small helpers, and the dep-rotator tool; no runtime application code is touched. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced ci/boot/bootstrap.sh and consolidated environment/credentials setup into a single entrypoint that is executed by lint, unit, and integration workflows; this reduces duplicated shell logic and lowers presubmit flake by standardizing PATH/KUBECONFIG handling. 2) Reworked ci/workflows/lint.yml and ci/workflows/test-matrix.yml to call the new bootstrap step and to expose a light-weight 'fastpath' lane for small PRs based on changed paths detection. 3) Added a minimal Go-based dep-rotator in tools/dep-rotator/ that runs static analysis against package manifests (go.mod, package.json) and outputs a proposed prune list; the rotator runs in dry-run mode by default and is gated behind a new label 'dep-approve' for auto-apply. 4) Added Makefile.ci with typed targets for common CI operations and documented the new flow in docs/ci/dep-policy.md and README.ci.md. 5) Small hygiene edits: removed obsolete helpers in scripts/ci-legacy-setup.sh, trimmed duplicated env vars in infra/helm/ci-values.yaml, and updated test runner docker image tag to reduce image-pull flakiness. Backwards compatibility and safety: bootstrap.sh has a strict dry-run / apply mode flag; workflows default to dry-run for dep-rotator; the fastpath triggers are conservative and require at least one approving reviewer for release branches. Rollout plan: roll out on canary for the monorepo (team-redwood/*) for 48 hours, then opt-in teams can flip 'fastpath' label for faster feedback. If any presubmit flake increases by >3% over baseline we will revert the fastpath lane while keeping the bootstrap consolidation. Checklist: [x] consolidated shell logic into single bootstrap entrypoint; [x] added Makefile.ci and docs; [x] dep-rotator initial implementation with dry-run; [x] added tests for boot sequence idempotency; [x] manual smoke run on staging CI; [x] coordinated with infra for image tag bump. Known limitations: dep-rotator is conservative and does not auto-edit transitive lockfiles yet; future iteration will include language-specific heuristics and a vetting dashboard. CI summary: initial run had a lint flake on macOS runner, fixed by pinning a brew package; subsequent runs passed full matrix. Related: ENG-1924 tracks the ci velocity improvements target, ENG-2001 captures repo-level dep hygiene initiative.

Evan Turner: Rotator now detects repository root and falls back to per-submodule manifest discovery; dry-run results are posted to the PR as an artifact.

notes: This PR targeted decreased presubmit flakiness and shorter feedback loops. Post-merge monitoring: runbook created in docs/ci/post-merge-monitoring.md and will be observed for 72 hours. No breaking changes to runtime code. If dep-rotator identifies high-risk removals, a follow-up PR will surface a one-click rollback plan.
